national_adoption.clause: Seventh Schedule, Heading A, Part II, para 3(6) / Table 20
deviations: The Indian text states 'The maximum permissible errors during inspection shall be twice the maximum permissible errors allowed on verification', identical in effect to OIML 3.5.2.

load_definition: m is the load expressed in verification scale intervals, i.e. m = L / e where L is the true test load.
mpe_sign_note: The absolute value of the mpe is 0.5 e, 1.0 e or 1.5 e; the tabulated value carries no sign (Table 6, Note 1).

derived_rules.band_breakpoints_note: Test loads should include the loads at which the mpe changes band (A.4.4.1). A load point generator must place points at, or immediately either side of, each breakpoint.
derived_rules.multi_interval_note: For multi-interval instruments the mpe is determined from the verification scale interval ei of the partial range in which the load falls (3.3, worked example).
derived_rules.rounding_error_rule: The rounding error included in any digital indication shall be eliminated if d > 0.2 e (3.5.3.2). This is what the changeover-point procedure of A.4.4.3 achieves.
derived_rules.net_value_rule: The mpe applies to the net value for every possible tare load, except preset tare values (3.5.3.3).
derived_rules.tare_device_rule: The mpe for a tare weighing device is the same, for any tare value, as that of the instrument for the same value of load (3.5.3.4).
derived_rules.repeatability_rule: The difference between the results of several weighings of the same load shall not be greater than the absolute value of the mpe of the instrument for that load (3.6.1).
derived_rules.single_result_rule: Regardless of what variation of results is permitted, the error of any single weighing result shall by itself not exceed the mpe for the given load (3.6).

symbols.dL: sum of the additional small weights (each of e/10) added until the indication increases by one increment
symbols.L: true value of the test load
symbols.E0: error determined at or near zero load
symbols.Ec: error corrected for the zero error; Ec is the value compared against the mpe
